en: Oṃ! Homage to the one who possesses a mass of solar digits, who removes the body of time, who is the foundation for both the support and the supported, and who brings about existence while bestowing non-existence. (Cakrabheda-stotra 1)
Homage to Śiva, whose form is unmanifest, whose body is supreme bliss, and who wears as a garland the digits of the young moon and the lotus.
Homage to Hara, the Supreme Self, who causes the dissolution and separation of the mass of the flood of bonds,
and who abides within the womb of the essence of mantra.

Although you transcend all qualities and are beyond the reach even of the Lord of Speech, nevertheless, my speech is ever intent upon praising you from the very depths of my heart. (Cakrabhārastava 4)
O Lord whose face is everywhere, I am rendered helpless by the intense immersion in the flavor of devotion; since I am impelled by You, O Protector, there is no fault in me whatsoever.
O Śrīkaṇṭha, accept from me this unartificial worship of devotion, offered by one whose funeral ashes are purified by the dust of your lotus feet.
Having bathed within the sacred ford known as the Lotus of the Heart, which is frequented by yoginīs, and having washed my garments with the water of perfect awakening, I worship Śyāmakaṇṭha.
O Mahākāla, with the abundant blood produced from living beings, an offering vessel is made for you upon the trunk of a corpse.
Whatever web of conceptual constructions there may be for the apprehension of external objects—each such family of gate-keepers should be honored by the wise. (Cakrabheda-stotra 9)
O Beloved of the Daughter of the Mountain, you are worshipped within the secret sphere of deep sleep, which is liberated from all obscurations,
during the eclipse of the moon and the sun.

O Lord of the Three Worlds, the seat is that which is free from the delusions of existence and non-existence, and from the undertaking of rejection, acceptance, and arising, and is established in pure cognition alone.
O Lord of the World, I offer this gift of the form, augmented by the manifestation of the power of non-appearance, established upon the pedestal of the Fourth State.

For one whose mind is free from the stain of the measurement of direction, time, and place, what wise person would perform the invocation and dismissal of the Immovable One (Sthāṇu)? Cakrabheda-stava 13.
Having churned the ocean of power with the two eyes of the sun and the moon,
I offer this anointing with the essence of supreme nectar to Śiva.
Regarding the sense faculties and their objects that follow after passion and greed, you possess a lack of attachment, mastery, and a dry, cleansing powder. (Cakrabhūti 15)
Having quickly purified the bindu-tīrtha with the tip of the blade of kuśa grass,
one should offer that bath of the nectar of cessation to the one whose crest is the crescent moon.
Having applied the friction of the garment of the vast expanse of the sky of our own awakening to the transformations of your consciousness, we transform them. (Cakrabheda-stotra 17)
Flowing like a mountain torrent from the relinquishing of both knowledge and the object of knowledge, this stainless water for washing your feet bestows supreme bliss within me. Cakrabheda-stotra 18.

O All-pervading Lord, receive this sipping-water (ācamana) consisting of the flowing water of absolute liberation (kaivalya), which issues from the cave-sanctuary of the throbbing flow of the outpouring of intense bliss.
Having washed the pearl of the five knots with the waters of concentration,
O Vṛṣākapi, I offer this priceless oblation at your feet.

O Lord of the Mountain, you are worshipped with the flowers of praise consisting of the threefold speech, which are saturated with the fragrance of consciousness blossoming in the garden of the Fourth State (turya).
O Consort of the Mountain-Born, your incense, with a luster resembling the wick of an incense-stick, shines as it pierces the aperture of Brahma with the weapon of the flame of the life-force fire.
That unstruck sound which resounds within, the supreme cow in the highest abode—that bell, pregnant with the meaning of the texts, is sounded before Śambhu. (Cakrabheda-stotra 23)
O Blessed One, I kindle the flame of power blazing from the fire at the root, resembling the wick of a lamp, for the sake of dispelling the darkness of delusion.
May the moon of the digit of nectar that abandons worldly existence, belonging to the one who wears the moon as a crest-jewel, serve as an ointment for the liberation of those seeking release.
O Rudra, may that abode, arisen from the power of Nāda and free from the three impurities, be your crown-protuberance, which has cast away the bolt of the sky.
May the stainless lotus of Brahman, blossoming upon the ocean of your heart which has been drenched by the nectar-shower of devotion to You, be the crest-jewel upon Your head. (Cakrabhaktistotra 27)
The multitude of the lotuses of awakening is your necklace of pearls;
the digit of the moon is your portion that eternally rises and pervades within.
O Lord of the World, having drawn forth from the lotus of the universal space with the solar rays of Śakti, taste the flowing nectar of the moon of consciousness! CakBhst_29 //
Having placed the mantra in the mind, that [mind] in its power, and that [power] eternally risen in one's own abode,
one should properly perform the rite of recitation and offer it to Śiva.
O Dhūrjaṭi, when all objects are either completely relinquished or grasped within the immeasurable light,
I bind the mudrā of supreme pervasion, which is stainless.
The sound that unfolds here when one blocks the ears with the thumbs is song;
then, from the striking together of the first pair [of hands], there is instrumental music.

Intoxicated by the majesty of the *tāṇḍava* dance through the immersion in the aesthetic flavor (*rasa*) of existence, I roar within the path of mantra; what need is there for contemplations on external objects?
I have prepared a canopy for Śambhu above, with the sky of the contemplation of Śiva-nature, whose form is an unbroken circle.
Having caused the wheel of light to descend through the aperture of the crown from the sky of my heart,
I hold it before Dhūrjaṭi like a beautiful chowrie.
O Lord, you are fanned before you by the breezes from the swans' wings, which issue forth and spread out from the tips of the chambers of your nostrils like palm-leaf fans.
O noble-minded one, we now hold for you this parasol, which is free from all heat and white with the nectar of devotion to you.
By abandoning the stable of possessiveness, that horse of egoism— capable of drawing in the three worlds—
has been prepared for you as a mount.
This betel, radiant with the leaves of the *nāgavallī* creeper— the bliss of the joy of self-awareness—
and fragrant with the shimmering moon of the throbbing *spanda*, is offered to you.

I offer as an oblation within the fire of non-duality— the treasure-trove of Śiva and the source of all blessings— the accumulated fuel of latent impressions arising from the distinction between the enjoyer and the enjoyed.
Holding the ladle of *unmanā* with the hands of light and space,
I offer into the fire of the Unborn that which is filled with the fat dripping from merit and demerit.
May your wish-fulfilling jewel of a mind be mine for the rite of inner man-making, colored by the rays of the moon that is your meditation.
Having placed this consecrated [offering] in the lotus-hand of the Fortune of Liberation,
O Blessed One, I present it as the sacrificial fee consisting of my very life and all my possessions.
May the virtuous, desiring to cross to the further shore of the ocean of saṃsāra,
take refuge in the lofty raft of devotional worship of the Moon-crested Lord.
By whatever merit has been acquired through this praise of the feet of Īśāna, may the entire world be liberated from the fault of hatred. (CakBhst 45)
O Supreme Lord, Witness of the Universe, accept this hymn from me, whose mental fluctuations have abandoned regard for honor or dishonor,
whose crest is bowed at the seat of Your pair of feet, whose body is smeared with ashes, and who holds a human skull in his hand.
Having rested in the Mahāpāśupata grove, a certain ascetic performed supreme praise and meditation upon Śambhu, the Lord of the Wheel of Consciousness.
